Basic Information

  • Full Programme Name: King's College London Joint PhD Scholarships
  • Host Institution: King's College London
  • Partner Universities: National University of Singapore (NUS), University of Hong Kong (HKU), University of São Paulo (USP)
  • Study Level: PhD
  • Start Date: 2026/27
  • Funding Type: Fully Funded
  • Tuition Fees: Full tuition fees
  • Stipend: Annual stipend (£22,780)
  • Research Grant: £1,000–£5,000
  • Eligibility: International PhD applicants
  • Application Deadline: Varies by partner; tentative December 2026 – February 2027

Project Overview & Significance

The King's Doctoral College offers highly Joint PhD Scholarships for candidates undertaking joint PhD programmes between King's College London and four of its esteemed international partner universities: the National University of Singapore (NUS), the University of Hong Kong (HKU), and the University of São Paulo (USP). These scholarships represent a unique opportunity to pursue a truly global doctoral education. Students will split their time between King's in London and their chosen partner institution, gaining exposure to diverse academic cultures, research facilities, and international networks. This dual-location approach significantly enriches the research experience and prepares graduates for international academic and industry careers.

Research Themes & Objectives

Because these scholarships are available across multiple faculties, the research themes are vast and varied, spanning sciences, engineering, humanities, and social sciences. The core objective is to foster collaborative research that leverages the specific strengths and expertise of both King's and the partner university. Successful candidates will develop a global perspective on their research topic, learning to navigate and synthesise different methodological approaches and cultural contexts.

Training & Development

Joint PhD students are part of an elite cohort. They benefit from the extensive training and development opportunities offered by the King's Doctoral College, as well as those provided by the partner institution. The inclusion of a research grant (ranging from £1,000 to £5,000) specifically supports international travel, conference attendance, and fieldwork, ensuring students can fully maximise the resources of both universities. Graduates emerge with a joint degree, signifying their ability to operate at the highest levels of international research.

Eligibility & Requirements

These scholarships are specifically aimed at international PhD applicants. Candidates must apply and be accepted into a joint PhD programme between King's and one of the partner universities. Academic excellence is paramount, and applicants must demonstrate a strong research proposal that justifies the collaborative, transnational nature of the joint programme.

How to Apply

Prospective candidates must first apply to the relevant joint PhD programme through the King's application system. Following programme application, students should follow the specific scholarship application instructions outlined on the King's College London scholarships page before the respective partner deadlines.
